subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be repaired as the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding per-agent compaction/context-pruning changes public config, provider routing, and session-state semantics, so automation should not create a competing fix before maintainer intent is clear.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and repair or replace the open PR as the landing path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` for now and defer the broader compaction/contextPruning merge surface to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the implementation PRs, leaving users to use global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve the config direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and repair or replace the open PR as the landing path.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent commits on the agent config schema, agent-scope helpers, and adjacent compaction cleanup where this public contract would land.
